newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Five kilos of TNT found on Belgrade-Vienna express.
newsitem.headline: Five kilos of TNT found on Belgrade-Vienna express.

text.p: Hungarian border guards said on Saturday they had discovered five kg (11 lbs) of explosives hidden on the overnight express train from Belgrade to Vienna.

The explosives, which the guards said were enough to destroy an apartment building , were detected by a sniffer dog. They were hidden in two nylon bags locked in a cupboard in the passageway between two coaches.

"It's a train we regularly check for drugs, human smuggling and weapons," border guard spokesman Attila Krisan told Reuters. "The train crossed the border at 23.10 last night and this time we found 10 packages of plastic industrial explosives and three metres of fuse.
"It was certainly one of the biggest amount of high explosives we've found in one place -- it could cause a terrible amount of destruction."
Krisan said it was impossible to know who had planted the packages. No arrests were made and all 53 passengers on the train, mainly Austrians and Yugoslavs, were allowed to continue their journey.
He added it was unlikely the train was the target.
"The TNT wasn't wired up and there were a number of stops on the route where the bags could have been unloaded." he said.
The train was due to cross Hungary into Austria but was not scheduled to stop in any of the Hungarian capital Budapest's main stations.

Krisan said it was too early to link the find to a recent spate of pipe bomb and grenade attacks in Hungary which have claimed two lives and caused thousands of dollars worth of damage, mainly to restaurants and night clubs.
In the latest incident on Friday, police defused a large device placed under the car of a Hungarian businessman with U.S. citizenship after the package was discovered by his wife.
